title: Impact of Class Size Cap Policy on Reading Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

The data structure is a classic DID setup with:
- A treatment group (schools subject to class size cap policy) and a control group
- Pre-period and post-period observations
- A pre-computed interaction term (`treat_x_post`) capturing the DID estimator

The key identifying assumption is the **parallel trends assumption**: absent the class size cap policy, treated and control schools would have experienced the same trends in reading scores over time. This is plausible if the policy assignment was not correlated with differential pre-existing trends in reading performance.

The DID estimator isolates the causal effect by differencing out:
1. Time-invariant differences between treated and control schools (school fixed effects)
2. Common time shocks affecting all schools equally

## 2. R Code

```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s45_data.csv")

# ---- Explore the data ----
cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(df), "rows,", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("\nTreatment/Period breakdown:\n")
print(table(treated = df$treated, post = df$post))

cat("\nSummary statistics for y by group:\n")
tapply(df$y, list(Treated = df$treated, Post = df$post), function(x) {
  sprintf("mean=%.3f, sd=%.3f, n=%d", mean(x), sd(x), length(x))
})
print(tapply(df$y, list(Treated = df$treated, Post = df$post), mean))

# ---- Main DID Regression ----
cat("\n=== Main DID Specification ===\n")
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(did_model)

# Robust standard errors (HC1)
cat("\n=== DID with Robust Standard Errors (HC1) ===\n")
robust_se <- coeftest(did_model, vcov = vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_se)

# Extract key DID coefficient
did_coef <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
did_se <- robust_se["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
did_pval <- robust_se["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("\n=== KEY RESULT ===\n")
cat(sprintf("DID Estimate (ATT): %.4f SD units\n", did_coef))
cat(sprintf("Robust SE: %.4f\n", did_se))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", did_coef - 1.96*did_se, did_coef + 1.96*did_se))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", did_pval))

# ---- Manual DID Calculation (Verification) ----
cat("\n=== Manual DID Verification ===\n")
means <- tapply(df$y, list(df$treated, df$post), mean)
manual_did <- (means["1","1"] - means["1","0"]) - (means["0","1"] - means["0","0"])
cat(sprintf("Manual DID: %.4f\n", manual_did))
cat(sprintf("Treated: Pre=%.4f, Post=%.4f, Diff=%.4f\n", 
            means["1","0"], means["1","1"], means["1","1"] - means["1","0"]))
cat(sprintf("Control: Pre=%.4f, Post=%.4f, Diff=%.4f\n", 
            means["0","0"], means["0","1"], means["0","1"] - means["0","0"]))

# ---- Robustness Check 1: Clustered SEs at school level (if panel) ----
cat("\n=== Robustness: HC2 Standard Errors ===\n")
robust_hc2 <- coeftest(did_model, vcov = vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC2"))
print(robust_hc2)

# ---- Robustness Check 2: Placebo test - effect in pre-period ----
cat("\n=== Robustness: Pre-treatment group balance ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
pre_test <- t.test(y ~ treated, data = pre_data)
cat(sprintf("Pre-treatment mean difference: %.4f (p=%.4f)\n", 
            diff(rev(pre_test$estimate)), pre_test$p.value))

# ---- Robustness Check 3: Simple model without controls ----
cat("\n=== Robustness: Only interaction term with FE-style ===\n")
did_model2 <- lm(y ~ factor(treated) * factor(post), data = df)
print(coeftest(did_model2, vcov = vcovHC(did_model2, type = "HC1")))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign:** **Positive** — Class size reduction policies are generally associated with improved student outcomes. The literature (e.g., Tennessee STAR experiment) finds that smaller classes improve reading performance.

**Expected magnitude:** Approximately **0.1 to 0.3 SD units**. The STAR experiment found effects of roughly 0.15-0.25 SD for early grades. Given this is an observational DID study, the effect could be somewhat attenuated or amplified depending on the intensity of the class size reduction.

**Statistical significance:** With 100 observations split across 4 cells (~25 per cell), power may be moderate. We expect the effect to be detectable if it is meaningfully large (≥0.2 SD), but marginal effects may not reach statistical significance at conventional levels.

**Pre-treatment balance:** We expect no significant difference in pre-period trends between treated and control schools if the parallel trends assumption holds.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Comparative analysis of reading scores before and after the policy in treated and untreated schools.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The class size cap policy resulted in a decrease in reading scores.
